title: Two weaknesses
line: One weakness can be defended. Two usually cannot.

steps.text: Your passed pawn on d5 is guarded by a pawn. Black's king stands in front of it. That one weakness Black can hold.
Make a second weakness on the other side. Push the pawn on g3 one square, ready to break up Black's pawns there.

wrong.a3a4: That plays on the side where Black's king already stands guard.

steps.after: Black's king heads over to that side.

steps.text: Bring your next pawn up beside it.
steps.after: Black's king comes closer to help.
Black gives a pawn, with check, to break up your pawns.
Black takes your other pawn. You now have two passed pawns.

steps.text: Push the passed pawn on d5. Black's king has to watch two passed pawns at once.

also.e4f3: That is as strong. This lesson pushes the pawn the king has left.
also.e4f4: That is as strong. This lesson pushes the pawn the king has left.

steps.after: Black's king stands between your two pawns and cannot be next to both.

summary: A defender can hold one weakness. Make a second one far from the first, and the defense gives way.
